questions.stem: What is the primary function of the semilunar valves in the heart?
choices: To allow the flow of blood in one direction
To allow the flow of blood in both directions
To increase the pressure of blood
To decrease the pressure of blood
questions.solution: The semilunar valves are structured to open and close in response to pressure changes, ensuring that blood flows in one direction through the heart. This prevents backflow, which is essential for maintaining efficient circulation. The other options incorrectly suggest the valves control blood flow direction or alter pressure, which is not their primary function.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of plasma in blood?
choices: It helps in the clotting of blood
It carries oxygen to all parts of the body
It helps in the transport of nutrients and waste
It destroys foreign organisms entering the body
questions.solution: Plasma is the fluid part of blood that helps in the transport of nutrients, waste, and other substances. It does not carry oxygen directly, as that is the role of red blood cells. Plasma also contains clotting factors, but clotting is a function of platelets and specific proteins, not plasma itself. Destroying foreign organisms is the role of white blood cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of red blood cells in the human circulatory system?
choices: Carry oxygen to body cells
Fight infections
Clot blood
Produce antibodies
questions.solution: Red blood cells carry oxygen to body cells because they contain hemoglobin, which binds to oxygen in the lungs and releases it in tissues. White blood cells fight infections, platelets clot blood, and antibodies are produced by specialized white blood cells, not red blood cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of an Rh-ve individual?
choices: They have Rh antigens on their RBCs
They never form antibodies against Rh antigens
They form antibodies if exposed to Rh+ve blood
They always have a higher blood volume
questions.solution: An Rh-ve individual lacks the Rh antigen on their red blood cells. If exposed to Rh+ve blood, their immune system produces antibodies against the Rh antigen. This is why Rh compatibility is crucial for blood transfusions. The other options are incorrect because Rh-ve individuals do not have Rh antigens, do form antibodies upon exposure, and blood volume is not directly related to Rh status.

questions.stem: If a person has blood group AB, which of the following blood groups can they receive?
choices: Only group A
Only group B
Only group AB
Any blood group
questions.solution: Persons with blood group AB can receive blood from any other blood group because they do not have antibodies against A or B antigens. This makes them 'universal recipients'. The other options are incorrect because group AB individuals can receive blood from A, B, AB, or O groups, not just AB. Group O can only receive O blood, and groups A and B can only receive their own or O.

hi.critique: The translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses standard Hindi medical terminology.

mr.stem: जर एखाद्या व्यक्तीचा रक्तगट AB असेल, तर खालीलपैकी कोणता रक्तगट त्यांना देता येईल?

O गटाच्या व्यक्तींना केवळ O गटाचा रक्त दिला जाऊ शकतो आणि A आणि B गटांच्या व्यक्तींना त्यांचा स्वतःचा किंवा O गटाचा रक्त दिला जाऊ शकतो.

questions.stem: What is the function of the hepatic portal system in the human circulatory system?
choices: To carry blood from the liver to the heart
To carry blood from the digestive tract to the liver
To carry blood from the liver to the lungs
To carry blood from the liver to the kidneys
questions.solution: The hepatic portal system carries blood from the digestive tract to the liver, allowing the liver to process nutrients and toxins before they enter the general circulation. This function is essential for regulating substances absorbed from the digestive system. The other options describe incorrect routes of blood flow that do not align with the known role of the hepatic portal system.

questions.stem: In which part of the circulatory system does the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide occur?

Arteries
Veins
Capillaries
questions.solution: Capillaries are the tiny blood vessels where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged between the blood and body tissues due to their thin walls, which allow for easy diffusion. Alveoli are part of the respiratory system, not the circulatory system, and are where gas exchange occurs between air and blood in the lungs.
